rows.currentScript: Look at lines 22 and 23, where Mrs Otis speaks. She says 'something has been spilt there'. Her words before that are a polite way of speaking, not fear. Line 22 says she did not know 'what it really signified'. Mrs Umney names Lady Eleanore later, on line 29, not Mrs Otis.
rows.whyRewrite: Last sentence 'Mrs Umney names Lady Eleanore later, on line 29, not Mrs Otis.' reads naturally as Mrs Umney naming Lady Eleanore rather than naming Mrs Otis; it needs to say it is Mrs Umney, not Mrs Otis, who names her. 'Her words before that are a polite way of speaking' leaves the words unquoted: quote 'I am afraid' (l.22). And 'she did not know what it really signified' (l.22) points the child at the content of option A ('Something she was quite unconscious of') without setting it aside as not what she takes the stain to be. Quotations are otherwise verbatim.
